prompt: Set up AI search over my notes so I can ask questions by meaning, not keywords.
context: Vault at /Users/me/Vault, Python 3.11 available, no index yet, works offline required.
rubric: Installs the requirements (`pip install -r requirements.txt`: sentence-transformers, faiss-cpu, numpy, pyyaml, tqdm)
Mentions `--action update` for incremental re-indexing of new or modified notes
anti_patterns: Recommends uploading the vault to a hosted embedding service
Rebuilds the full index for every incremental change
gold_notes: sentence-transformers + FAISS, three actions: build, ask, update.

prompt: Add 'call the accountant' to today's tasks.
context: Vault at /Users/me/Vault, Obsidian running, daily notes enabled.
rubric: Uses `obsidian daily:append content="- [ ] Call the accountant"`
Writes the task in Obsidian checkbox syntax
Mentions `obsidian tasks todo` / `obsidian tasks daily` to review tasks afterwards
Keeps the answer short — this is a one-command operation
anti_patterns: Opens and rewrites the daily note file by hand while the app is running
Turns a one-line capture into a vault-wide workflow
gold_notes: Task ref toggling: `obsidian task ref="Note.md:8" toggle`.

prompt: Pull this article into my vault as a note: https://example.com/an-article
rubric: Mentions the ingestion modes (note, append, daily-append, split) and picks the right one
Adds frontmatter (source URL, created date, tags) so the note is findable later
Mentions the supported source formats when the user has local files instead
anti_patterns: Pastes the article body with no frontmatter or source attribution
Invents an ingest flag the script does not have

prompt: Update the frontmatter of 200 notes from a CI job.
context: GitHub Actions runner, vault checked out as a git repo, Obsidian app not installed.
rubric: Chooses the file-based approach because the Obsidian CLI needs the running app
Uses `bulk_properties.py` (or direct YAML frontmatter edits) rather than `obsidian` commands
States explicitly that `obsidian` CLI commands are unavailable in CI
Relies on git for the safety net (diff review, revert) instead of a manual backup
anti_patterns: Suggests `obsidian property:set` in a headless CI environment
Ignores that the vault is version-controlled and adds a redundant backup step
gold_notes: Decision table: CLI when the app runs; file-based for CI/CD and bulk work.
